reason: Verified by driving, not by selector. Loaded ?state=owner-empty, typed '3 October 2026', pressed 'Set the day', and harvested document.body.textContent in full: 'Aisling & Tom / 79 / days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Nothing sits between today and the day yet. Everything you add is measured from it. / Add a moment / The day is set. Moments come next. / Kept by Orla / Signal Timeline'. The only occurrence of the string 'today' on the whole page is the deictic one inside .b-emptyBody; 'Today is', 'Today,' and '16 July' appear nowhere, in visible text or in the accessible tree. A computed-style sweep for rgb(79,70,229) over every element returns zero hits, so the screen carries no indigo either. The foot is built with stamp:false, so there is no 'Updated' date to anchor it by accident. This is a literal instance of the paid-for class in lessons.md line 69 - 'If anything shows a date, somewhere on screen states today' - and it is aggravated, not merely technical: the body copy uses the word 'today' as its reference point on a screen that never says what today is, so the one sentence explaining the number leans on an unstated now. Compare the same builder's own horizon(), which on owner-flight, phone and desk emits .b-todayRule + .b-todayLabel 'Today is 16 July' and the row's 'Today, 16 July'; the setday replacement block at render-b.js ~1362 rebuilds b-who + countBlock + .b-when and drops both. Not restated by either gate: interaction-check.mjs drives this exact path four times (lines 671-700, 1498, 1956, 2266) and asserts only that the form stops asking, that .b-num is > 0, that 'Add a moment' takes focus and that the hint announces - nothing about today; the .b-todayRule assertions at 1881 and 2477 run on owner-flight geometry, never here. No constraint is broken: .b-todayRule and .b-todayLabel are ratified indigo and mono-label uses already in the lock, no new hue, no new weight, no architecture change. No conflict with round 8's other today findings: taste--pinned-label-stops-naming-what-is-under-it explicitly proposes to 'keep both statements of today and separate the registers', and type--stranded-function-words objects to where the printed today WRAPS, not to its existing; nothing in round 8 argues today is stated too often, and round 7 refuted deleting either statement. I injected the sharpened fix live and shot it at 1440, 768 and 390: the rule holds its 344px constant width inside the 1068px empty block exactly as it does in the horizon, the label sits at --fore-62 in mono above the body copy, and the sentence beneath it now has the referent it was already assuming. The only cost is 33px: at 1440 the answered screen goes from fitting the fold exactly (960) to 993. At 1280 and 1024 it already overflowed (944) before the fix, and at 390 the document height is unchanged. Two nodes, one file, one line each.
sharpenedFix: The fix is right but names two identifiers that do not exist and would throw on the owner's first action: there is no .b-todayLine class in b.css and no F.fmt.dayMonth in fixture.js (fmt exposes long, longYear, medium, short, numeral, monthShort, dayCount, weekdayShort, year), so F.fmt.dayMonth(F.today) is a TypeError inside the setday click handler and would leave the screen frozen on the form. Use the horizon's actual pair. In the 'next' block at render-b.js ~1362, between h('p.b-when', ...) and h('p.b-emptyBody', ...), insert exactly: h('div.b-todayRule'), h('p.b-todayLabel', { text: 'Today is ' + F.fmt.medium(F.today) }) - which renders 'Today is 16 July' with the same U+00A0 the rest of the document uses, in the same mono label register as owner-flight, with the rule's --accent, margins and 344px cap inherited rather than restated. Nothing else changes; do not touch the .b-emptyBody wording, which now reads correctly against a stated now. Add one line to the existing gate block at interaction-check.mjs:671-700 so the class cannot come back a third time: after 'the answer is announced', assert /Today is/.test(document.querySelector('.b-empty').textContent) and that .b-empty .b-todayRule exists. If the 33px of new scroll at 1440 is unwanted, take it out of .b-empty's 120px bottom padding at b.css:1291 rather than out of the anchor.
